Department of Computer Engineering, PESMCOE, Pune, India
Shraddha Dashpute, Hemant Choudhary, Sankalp Gaikwad, Priyanshu Jadhav, Balaji
P.E.S. Modern College of Engineering, Pune– 411005

- In today’s digital world, prolonged screen exposure among students and employees often leads to mental fatigue, stress, and reduced productivity. Traditional productivity tools fail to monitor emotional well-being, focusing only on time and task completion. This paper presents

, a real-time emotion-based productivity monitoring system that detects emotions and fatigue levels using facial expressions. The system employs computer vision and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) trained on the FER-2013 dataset to classify emotions such as happiness, sadness, and anger from webcam input. Based on continuous emotional trends, it identifies fatigue and provides real-time suggestions to help users regain focus. The results are visualized on a

dashboard, allowing users to track emotional patterns and productivity over time. This approach bridges the gap between emotional awareness and performance enhancement, promoting mental wellness and efficiency in digital workspaces.

In today’s digital era, students and employees spend long hours in front of computers for learning and professional work. Continuous screen exposure and mental load often lead to fatigue, stress, and reduced productivity — problems that typically go unnoticed until performance declines. While numerous studies have explored emotion detection and engagement analysis using facial expressions and deep learning, most systems fail to provide real-time feedback or actionable insights to users. This gap between emotion recognition and user well-being inspired the development of

, a system that not only detects emotions and fatigue levels but also assists users in maintaining focus through intelligent suggestions and visual feedback. The motivation behind this survey is to study existing techniques, understand their limitations, and highlight how real-
time, emotion-aware systems can improve cognitive performance and digital wellness.

To develop a real-time emotion-based productivity monitoring system that uses facial expression analysis through deep learning to detect fatigue and emotional fluctuations, and provides intelligent feedback or suggestions to help users maintain focus, reduce mental fatigue, and enhance overall productivity.
The main objective of this survey paper is to review and

existing research studies related to facial emotion recognition and fatigue detection using deep learning and computer vision techniques. It aims to examine the strengths and limitations of current emotion-based systems designed for engagement or productivity monitoring. The paper identifies key research gaps, such as the lack of real-time feedback, visualization, and adaptive user support in existing models. To address these gaps, the proposed system,

, is introduced as an advanced approach that integrates real-time emotion detection, fatigue analysis, and intelligent suggestion generation to enhance user focus and mental well-being. Ultimately, the objective is to demonstrate how

solution for maintaining productivity and emotional balance in digital environments.

Existing studies on emotion and engagement detection have made significant progress in facial expression recognition using deep learning, yet several critical gaps remain. Most research primarily focuses on emotion classification accuracy but fails to translate emotional data into actionable feedback or suggestions for improving user productivity and
well-being. Many systems rely on high-end GPUs or multimodal inputs (e.g., gaze, EEG, keystrokes), making them difficult to deploy on regular laptops.

– Real-Time Emotion-Based Productivity Monitoring System successfully combines facial emotion detection, fatigue analysis, and real-time feedback to enhance focus and productivity among students and employees. By utilizing computer vision and a CNN-based model (Mini-

) trained on the FER-2013 dataset, the system accurately identifies user emotions and detects fatigue based on continuous emotional patterns. Unlike previous studies that focus solely on emotion classification,
provides personalized suggestions and a dashboard visualization to help users track their mental and emotional states over time.

In the future, the system can be extended by incorporating multimodal inputs such as voice tone, posture, or eye gaze for improved accuracy. Integration with wearable devices and AI based task schedulers can offer deeper cognitive insights and automated work-rest cycle adjustments. Cloud-based deployment and mobile application support can further enhance accessibility, making
a complete digital wellness and productivity management solution.
